correctness.rationale: Reconstructed super domination via omitted complement C: D is super dominating exactly for |C|≤1 or |C|=2 with omitted vertices in distinct non-singleton partite classes. In a super-coalition partition every partner pair leaves ≤2 omitted vertices, forcing ≤4 blocks. For four blocks, the partner graph has no isolates: a matching of size 2 forces all blocks singleton and G=K2,2; otherwise it is a 3-leaf star and those leaves must occupy three distinct parts of size≥2. Both conditions give explicit constructions; 3 blocks always possible at N≥3 by pairing complements of singletons. Exhaustive independently written direct-definition enumeration matched the formula for all connected complete multipartite part profiles of orders 2–7, corroborating but not replacing the proof.

value.rationale: An exact natural-family coalition-number classification with a sharp combinatorial threshold and a genuine universal-vertex counterexample to an asserted theorem. The star-versus-matching structure explains the four-block transition, beyond merely recomputing the known scalar super domination number.

final_claim: For any finite connected complete multipartite graph G=K_{n1,…,nr}, N≥2, p=#parts of size≥2, C_s(G)=0 if N=2, equals 4 if N≥3 and either p≥3 or G≅K2,2, and equals 3 otherwise. In particular K1,2,2,2 has a universal vertex yet C_s=4, contradicting the universal-vertex assertion in arXiv:2607.22686v1.
limitations: Connected complete multipartite graphs only; order-two exception important.
Arbitrary order rests on partner-graph proof; finite enumeration stops at order 7 in independent replay.
